subject: maths
title: Primary 6 Average
seo_title: P6 Average Worksheets: Free Primary 6 Maths with Answers (MOE Syllabus, PSLE Practice)
standard_text: Average as total value ÷ number of data; relationship between average, total value and number of data
meta_desc: Free P6 average worksheets: find the average, the total and a missing value, and solve PSLE-style word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Average = total value ÷ number of data
key_sub: The average of 7, 3, 6 and 4 is 20 ÷ 4 = 5. To work backwards, total value = average × number of data.
body_html:
What is an average?

An average tells you how much each item would have if the total were shared equally.

Average = total value ÷ number of data

Example 1

Find the average of 48, 52, 39, 45 and 61.

Total = 48 + 52 + 39 + 45 + 61 = 245. There are 5 numbers. 245 ÷ 5 = 49.

Answer: 49

Example 2

Siti spent $2.40, $1.80, $3.10 and $2.30 at the canteen on 4 days. What was the average amount she spent per day?

Total = $9.60. $9.60 ÷ 4 = $2.40.

Answer: $2.40

Total value = average × number of data

If you know the average, multiply to get the total. Most PSLE average questions start here.

Example 3

The average of 4 numbers is 27. Three of the numbers are 18, 35 and 24. What is the fourth number?

Total of 4 numbers = 4 × 27 = 108. The three numbers add up to 18 + 35 + 24 = 77. 108 − 77 = 31.

Answer: 31

When a value is added or removed

Find the old total and the new total. The difference is the value that was added or removed.

Example 4

The average age of 4 children is 10 years. When their aunt joins them, the average age increases by 6 years. How old is the aunt?

Old total = 4 × 10 = 40. New average = 10 + 6 = 16, so new total = 5 × 16 = 80. Aunt = 80 − 40 = 40.

Answer: 40 years

Average with the model method

When the numbers are compared, change the average into a total first. Then draw a model and use units.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Dividing by the wrong number of dataCount the data. A 0 (a day with no rain) is still a piece of data
Giving the total or the middle value as the averageAverage = total ÷ number of data
Dividing the average to find the totalTotal = average × number of data
Adding a new value straight onto the averageFind the old total, add the value, then divide by the new number of data
Using the average in a missing-value questionMultiply back to the total first, then subtract what you know
Finding the average of two averages for groups of different sizesFind each total, add them, then divide by everyone

faq.q: How do you find the average in P6 maths?
faq.a: Add all the values to get the total, then divide by the number of data. For 7, 3, 6 and 4 the total is 20, and 20 ÷ 4 = 5, so the average is 5.

faq.q: Is average tested in the PSLE?
faq.a: Yes. Average is part of the Primary 6 Statistics topic in the MOE syllabus, and PSLE questions often combine it with the model method, before-and-after changes or a bar graph.

faq.q: How do I solve a question where the average increases after someone joins?
faq.a: Find the old total (old average × old number) and the new total (new average × new number), then subtract. If 4 children have an average age of 10 and the average becomes 16 when an adult joins, the adult is 80 − 40 = 40 years old.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with averages?
faq.a: Forgetting to multiply back to the total. Questions about a missing value, a new value or two groups must be worked with totals, not with the averages themselves.

items.q: Kumar scored 17, 9, 19 and 15 marks in 4 spelling tests. Each test was out of 20. What was his average mark?
items.e: Total: 17 + 9 + 19 + 15 = 60. There are 4 tests. Average = 60 ÷ 4 = 15.

items.q: Hafiz read 32, 39, 34, 33 and 22 pages of a storybook on 5 nights. What was the average number of pages per night?
items.e: Total: 32 + 39 + 34 + 33 + 22 = 160. There are 5 nights. Average = 160 ÷ 5 = 32.

items.q: The numbers of pupils absent from Class 6A on 5 days were 1, 3, 0, 3 and 3. What was the average number of pupils absent per day?
items.e: Total: 1 + 3 + 0 + 3 + 3 = 10. There are 5 days (the 0 counts too). Average = 10 ÷ 5 = 2.

items.q: A hawker sold 46, 25, 29, 21 and 24 plates of chicken rice in the first hour on 5 days. What was the average number of plates sold per day?
items.e: Total: 46 + 25 + 29 + 21 + 24 = 145. There are 5 days. Average = 145 ÷ 5 = 29.

items.q: Three parcels have masses of 1 kg 230 g, 1 kg 320 g and 885 g. What is the average mass of a parcel?
The school football team scored 5, 1, 0, 3 and 1 goals in 5 matches. What was the average number of goals per match?
items.e: Total: 5 + 1 + 0 + 3 + 1 = 10. There are 5 matches (the 0 counts too). Average = 10 ÷ 5 = 2.

items.q: The numbers of pupils who went to the library during recess on 6 days were 36, 22, 29, 21, 40 and 26. What was the average number of pupils per day?
The masses of 4 durians are 1.7, 1.6, 2.4 and 1.9 kg. What is the average mass of a durian?
items.e: Total: 1.7 + 1.6 + 2.4 + 1.9 = 7.6. There are 4 durians. Average = 7.6 ÷ 4 = 1.9 kg.

items.q: Four bottles hold 1 ℓ 500 ml, 1 ℓ 250 ml, 900 ml and 1 ℓ 350 ml of water. What is the average volume of water in a bottle?
items.e: Change to millilitres: 1500 + 1250 + 900 + 1350 = 5000 ml. Average = 5000 ml ÷ 4 = 1250 ml = 1 ℓ 250 ml.

items.q: Hui Min spent $2.20, $2.40, $2.60, $2.70 and $3.00 at the school canteen on 5 school days. What was the average amount she spent per day?
The heights of 4 pupils are 1.46, 1.45, 1.53 and 1.48 m. What is their average height?
At a book fair, 4 storybooks cost $9.00, $13.60, $9.70 and $10.30. What was the average price of a storybook?
The bar graph shows the number of pupils absent from Class 6B each day. What was the average number of pupils absent per day?
items.e: Total: 4 + 0 + 5 + 4 + 2 = 15. There are 5 days (the 0 counts too). Average = 15 ÷ 5 = 3.

items.q: Mr Tan walked 10 837, 9798, 12 721 and 8968 steps on 4 days. What was the average number of steps he walked per day?
A school weather station recorded 22.3, 35.6, 21.4, 4.3 and 36.6 mm of rain on 5 days. What was the average daily rainfall?
During Chinese New Year, Ryan received 5 red packets with $10, $12, $8, $8 and $20. What was the average amount in a red packet?
items.e: Total: $10 + $12 + $8 + $8 + $20 = $58. There are 5 red packets. Average = $58 ÷ 5 = $11.60.

items.q: The bar graph shows the number of cups of bubble tea a shop sold from Monday to Friday. What was the average number of cups sold per day?
items.e: Total: 70 + 90 + 70 + 60 + 40 = 330. There are 5 days. Average = 330 ÷ 5 = 66.

items.q: A school concert was held on 3 nights. The audience on the 3 nights was 1255, 1385 and 1272 people. What was the average audience per night?
items.e: Total: 1255 + 1385 + 1272 = 3912. There are 3 nights. Average = 3912 ÷ 3 = 1304.

items.q: What was the average time taken by the 4 pupils?
What was the average amount of money raised by a class?

sets.title: Find the total from the average

items.q: The average of three numbers is 43. What is the total of the three numbers?
items.e: Total value = average × number of numbers = 43 × 3 = 129.

items.q: The average of four numbers is 59. What is the total of the four numbers?
items.e: Total value = average × number of numbers = 59 × 4 = 236.

items.q: The average of five numbers is 33. What is the total of the five numbers?
items.e: Total value = average × number of numbers = 33 × 5 = 165.

items.q: The average of six numbers is 19. What is the total of the six numbers?
items.e: Total value = average × number of numbers = 19 × 6 = 114.

items.q: The average mass of 8 bags of rice is 5.07 kg. What is the total mass of the bags?
items.e: Total value = average × number of bags = 5.07 kg × 8 = 40.56 kg.

items.q: The average of four numbers is 25.2. What is the total of the four numbers?
items.e: Total value = average × number of numbers = 25.2 × 4 = 100.8.

items.q: Ethan saved an average of $6.10 a week for 12 weeks. How much did he save altogether?
items.e: Total value = average × number of weeks = $6.10 × 12 = $73.20.

items.q: The average length of 6 ribbons is 36.1 cm. What is the total length of the ribbons?
items.e: Total value = average × number of ribbons = 36.1 cm × 6 = 216.6 cm.

items.q: Nurul spent an average of 65 min a day reading for 5 days. How much time did she spend altogether? Give your answer in hours and minutes.
items.e: Total = 65 min × 5 = 325 min. 325 min = 5 × 60 min + 25 min = 5 h 25 min.

items.q: The average of eight numbers is 16.9. What is the total of the eight numbers?
items.e: Total value = average × number of numbers = 16.9 × 8 = 135.2.

items.q: The average price of 4 T-shirts is $18.20. What is the total price of the T-shirts?
items.e: Total value = average × number of T-shirts = $18.20 × 4 = $72.80.

items.q: The average amount of water in 6 cups is 325 ml. How much water is there altogether?
The average height of 4 pupils in a relay team is 1.51 m. What is their total height?
items.e: Total value = average × number of pupils = 1.51 m × 4 = 6.04 m.

items.q: A stall sold 25 bowls of laksa. The average amount collected per bowl was $6.10. How much money did the stall collect?
items.e: Total value = average × number of bowls = $6.10 × 25 = $152.50.

items.q: Jun Jie’s total score in some tests was 370 marks. His average score was 74 marks. How many tests did he take?
items.e: Number of tests = total ÷ average = 370 ÷ 74 = 5.

items.q: Some boxes have a total mass of 60 kg. The average mass of a box is 7.5 kg. How many boxes are there?
items.e: Number of boxes = total ÷ average = 60 ÷ 7.5 = 8.

items.q: The average distance Arjun jogged each day for 7 days at East Coast Park was 4.3 km. How far did he jog altogether?
items.e: Total value = average × number of days = 4.3 km × 7 = 30.1 km.

items.q: Ali spent an average of 45 min a day practising the piano for a week. How much time did he spend altogether? Give your answer in hours and minutes.
items.e: Total = 45 min × 7 = 315 min. 315 min = 5 × 60 min + 15 min = 5 h 15 min.

items.q: A group of friends saved $102 altogether. The average amount each friend saved was $17. How many friends were there?
items.e: Number of friends = total ÷ average = 102 ÷ 17 = 6.

items.q: A class collected 128 cans for recycling. On average, each pupil collected 4 cans. How many pupils are in the class?
items.e: Number of pupils = total ÷ average = 128 ÷ 4 = 32.

items.q: The average of three numbers is 31. Two of the numbers are 19 and 33. What is the missing number?
items.e: Total of all 3 numbers = 31 × 3 = 93. The 2 numbers given add up to 19 + 33 = 52. Missing number = 93 − 52 = 41.

items.q: The average of four numbers is 28. Three of the numbers are 17, 30 and 26. What is the missing number?
items.e: Total of all 4 numbers = 28 × 4 = 112. The 3 numbers given add up to 17 + 30 + 26 = 73. Missing number = 112 − 73 = 39.

items.q: The average of two numbers is 45. One of the numbers is 30. What is the other number?
items.e: Total = 2 × 45 = 90. Other number = 90 − 30 = 60.

items.q: The average of four numbers is 14. Three of the numbers are 14, 9 and 16. What is the missing number?
items.e: Total of all 4 numbers = 14 × 4 = 56. The 3 numbers given add up to 14 + 9 + 16 = 39. Missing number = 56 − 39 = 17.

items.q: Kavya’s average mark for 3 tests was 80. Her marks for 2 of the tests were 72 and 69. What was her mark for the other test?
items.e: Total for 3 tests = 80 × 3 = 240. Known marks: 72 + 69 = 141. Other test = 240 − 141 = 99.

items.q: The average of five numbers is 24. Four of the numbers are 12, 22, 17 and 29. What is the missing number?
items.e: Total of all 5 numbers = 24 × 5 = 120. The 4 numbers given add up to 12 + 22 + 17 + 29 = 80. Missing number = 120 − 80 = 40.

items.q: Hafiz’s marks for 3 Science tests were 74, 71 and 80. What mark must he get in the next test so that his average mark for all 4 tests is 80?
items.e: Total needed for 4 tests = 4 × 80 = 320. Total so far = 74 + 71 + 80 = 225. Mark needed = 320 − 225 = 95.

items.q: The bar for Tuesday is missing. The average number of books borrowed per day was 31. How many books were borrowed on Tuesday?
items.e: Total = 31 × 5 = 155. The other bars add up to 45 + 20 + 25 + 40 = 130. Tuesday: 155 − 130 = 25.

items.q: The average of five numbers is 90. Four of the numbers are 89, 84, 78 and 85. What is the missing number?
items.e: Total of all 5 numbers = 90 × 5 = 450. The 4 numbers given add up to 89 + 84 + 78 + 85 = 336. Missing number = 450 − 336 = 114.

items.q: The average of two numbers is 17.8. One of the numbers is 4. What is the other number?
Chloe’s average mark for 4 tests was 82. Her marks for 3 of the tests were 63, 90 and 80. What was her mark for the other test?
items.e: Total for 4 tests = 82 × 4 = 328. Known marks: 63 + 90 + 80 = 233. Other test = 328 − 233 = 95.

items.q: The average of three numbers A, B and C is 63. The average of A and B is 71. What is C?
Priya’s marks for 4 Science tests were 66, 90, 85 and 83. What mark must she get in the next test so that her average mark for all 5 tests is 83?
items.e: Total needed for 5 tests = 5 × 83 = 415. Total so far = 66 + 90 + 85 + 83 = 324. Mark needed = 415 − 324 = 91.

items.q: The average of six numbers is 74. Five of the numbers are 71, 73, 65, 72 and 82. What is the missing number?
items.e: Total of all 6 numbers = 74 × 6 = 444. The 5 numbers given add up to 71 + 73 + 65 + 72 + 82 = 363. Missing number = 444 − 363 = 81.

items.q: The bar for May is missing. The average rainfall for the 5 months was 210 mm. What was the rainfall in May?
Kumar’s average mark for 5 tests was 76. His marks for 4 of the tests were 62, 70, 72 and 80. What was his mark for the other test?
items.e: Total for 5 tests = 76 × 5 = 380. Known marks: 62 + 70 + 72 + 80 = 284. Other test = 380 − 284 = 96.

items.q: The average of three numbers A, B and C is 20. The average of A and B is 22. What is C?
Xin Yi’s marks for 4 Science tests were 83, 74, 86 and 65. What mark must she get in the next test so that her average mark for all 5 tests is 81?
items.e: Total needed for 5 tests = 5 × 81 = 405. Total so far = 83 + 74 + 86 + 65 = 308. Mark needed = 405 − 308 = 97.

items.q: The average of three numbers A, B and C is 62. The average of A and B is 53. What is C?
The average of 5 numbers is 32. The average of the first 3 numbers is 48. What is the average of the last 2 numbers?
items.e: Total of 5 numbers = 5 × 32 = 160. Total of first 3 = 3 × 48 = 144. Last 2 add up to 160 − 144 = 16. Average = 16 ÷ 2 = 8.

sets.title: When a value is added or removed

items.q: The average of three numbers is 36. The number 60 is added to the group. What is the average of the four numbers now?
items.e: Old total = 36 × 3 = 108. New total = 108 + 60 = 168. New average = 168 ÷ 4 = 42.

items.q: The average of four numbers is 24. The number 51 is removed. What is the average of the remaining three numbers?
items.e: Old total = 24 × 4 = 96. New total = 96 − 51 = 45. New average = 45 ÷ 3 = 15.

items.q: The average of four numbers is 28. The number 53 is added to the group. What is the average of the five numbers now?
items.e: Old total = 28 × 4 = 112. New total = 112 + 53 = 165. New average = 165 ÷ 5 = 33.

items.q: The average of five numbers is 29. The number 69 is removed. What is the average of the remaining four numbers?
items.e: Old total = 29 × 5 = 145. New total = 145 − 69 = 76. New average = 76 ÷ 4 = 19.

items.q: The average of four numbers is 38. The number 53 is added to the group. What is the average of the five numbers now?
items.e: Old total = 38 × 4 = 152. New total = 152 + 53 = 205. New average = 205 ÷ 5 = 41.

items.q: The average of four numbers is 30. When one more number is added, the average becomes 35. What is the number that was added?
items.e: Old total = 4 × 30 = 120. New total = 5 × 35 = 175. Number added = 175 − 120 = 55.

items.q: The average of five numbers is 24. The number 60 is removed. What is the average of the remaining four numbers?
items.e: Old total = 24 × 5 = 120. New total = 120 − 60 = 60. New average = 60 ÷ 4 = 15.

items.q: The average of five numbers is 20. The number 14 is added to the group. What is the average of the six numbers now?
items.e: Old total = 20 × 5 = 100. New total = 100 + 14 = 114. New average = 114 ÷ 6 = 19.

items.q: The average of five numbers is 43. When one more number is added, the average becomes 48. What is the number that was added?
items.e: Old total = 5 × 43 = 215. New total = 6 × 48 = 288. Number added = 288 − 215 = 73.

items.q: The average of five numbers is 43. When one number is removed, the average of the remaining numbers is 40. What number was removed?
items.e: Old total = 5 × 43 = 215. New total = 4 × 40 = 160. Number removed = 215 − 160 = 55.

items.q: The average of six numbers is 30. The number 45 is removed. What is the average of the remaining five numbers?
items.e: Old total = 30 × 6 = 180. New total = 180 − 45 = 135. New average = 135 ÷ 5 = 27.

items.q: The average of six numbers is 18. The number 39 is added to the group. What is the average of the seven numbers now?
items.e: Old total = 18 × 6 = 108. New total = 108 + 39 = 147. New average = 147 ÷ 7 = 21.

items.q: The average of six numbers is 26. When one more number is added, the average becomes 28. What is the number that was added?
items.e: Old total = 6 × 26 = 156. New total = 7 × 28 = 196. Number added = 196 − 156 = 40.

items.q: The average of six numbers is 33. When one number is removed, the average of the remaining numbers is 37. What number was removed?
items.e: Old total = 6 × 33 = 198. New total = 5 × 37 = 185. Number removed = 198 − 185 = 13.

items.q: The average of seven numbers is 36. When one more number is added, the average becomes 41. What is the number that was added?
items.e: Old total = 7 × 36 = 252. New total = 8 × 41 = 328. Number added = 328 − 252 = 76.

items.q: The average of eight numbers is 41. When one number is removed, the average of the remaining numbers is 39. What number was removed?
items.e: Old total = 8 × 41 = 328. New total = 7 × 39 = 273. Number removed = 328 − 273 = 55.

items.q: Hui Min’s average score for 4 spelling tests was 13. Each test was out of 20. Later, her teacher found that one score of 9 should be 17. What is the correct average score?
items.e: The total increases by 17 − 9 = 8. Shared among 4 tests, the average increases by 8 ÷ 4 = 2. Correct average = 13 + 2 = 15.

items.q: The average of four numbers is 12. When one more number is added, the average increases by 3. What is the number that was added?
items.e: New average = 12 + 3 = 15. New total = 5 × 15 = 75. Old total = 4 × 12 = 48. Number added = 75 − 48 = 27.

items.q: The average of five numbers is 28. When one more number is added, the average increases by 2. What is the number that was added?
items.e: New average = 28 + 2 = 30. New total = 6 × 30 = 180. Old total = 5 × 28 = 140. Number added = 180 − 140 = 40.

items.q: Ryan’s average score for 5 spelling tests was 15. Each test was out of 20. Later, his teacher found that one score of 6 should be 16. What is the correct average score?
items.e: The total increases by 16 − 6 = 10. Shared among 5 tests, the average increases by 10 ÷ 5 = 2. Correct average = 15 + 2 = 17.

items.q: Wei Ming’s average mark for English, Maths and Science was 82. His mark for Mother Tongue was 90. What was his average mark for the 4 subjects?
items.e: Total for 3 subjects = 3 × 82 = 246. Total for 4 subjects = 246 + 90 = 336. Average = 336 ÷ 4 = 84.

items.q: A hawker sold an average of 85 plates of chicken rice a day from Monday to Friday. On Saturday and Sunday, he sold an average of 120 plates a day. What was the average number of plates he sold per day for the whole week?
items.e: Monday to Friday: 5 × 85 = 425. Weekend: 2 × 120 = 240. Week total = 665. Average = 665 ÷ 7 = 95.

items.q: The average age of 3 brothers is 9 years now. What will their average age be in 4 years’ time?
items.e: Each brother will be 4 years older, so the average also goes up by 4: 9 + 4 = 13 years. (Total now = 27; total then = 27 + 3 × 4 = 39; 39 ÷ 3 = 13.)

items.q: During one week in December, the average daily rainfall for the first 4 days was 12.6 mm. The average daily rainfall for the last 3 days was 4.2 mm. What was the average daily rainfall for the whole week?
items.e: First 4 days: 4 × 12.6 = 50.4 mm. Last 3 days: 3 × 4.2 = 12.6 mm. Total = 63 mm. Average = 63 ÷ 7 = 9 mm.

items.q: The average age of a family of 4 is 22 years. When their grandmother joins them, the average age of the 5 people increases by 10 years. How old is their grandmother?
items.e: Before: 4 × 22 = 88 years. After: the average is 22 + 10 = 32, so the total is 5 × 32 = 160 years. Grandmother = 160 − 88 = 72 years.

items.q: The average of two numbers is 45. One number is 18 more than the other. What is the bigger number?
items.e: Total = 2 × 45 = 90. 2 units = 90 − 18 = 72, so 1 unit = 36. Bigger number = 36 + 18 = 54.

items.q: In a class, the average mass of the 12 boys is 42 kg and the average mass of the 18 girls is 38 kg. What is the average mass of all the pupils in the class?
items.e: Boys: 12 × 42 = 504 kg. Girls: 18 × 38 = 684 kg. Total = 1188 kg for 30 pupils. Average = 1188 ÷ 30 = 39.6 kg. (Not (42 + 38) ÷ 2, because the groups are different sizes.)

items.q: Mr Tan is 3 times as old as his son. Their average age is 26 years. How old is Mr Tan?
items.e: Total age = 2 × 26 = 52 years. 4 units = 52, so 1 unit = 13. Mr Tan = 3 units = 39 years.

items.q: The average age of 5 pupils in a CCA group is 11 years. A coach joins the group, and the average age increases by 2 years. How old is the coach?
items.e: Total age of 5 pupils = 5 × 11 = 55. New total = 6 × 13 = 78. Coach = 78 − 55 = 23 years. (The coach is 10 years older than the new average, enough to add 2 years to each of the 5 pupils.)

items.q: The average height of 5 basketball players is 1.62 m. One player leaves the team. The average height of the other 4 players is 1.60 m. What is the height of the player who left?
Farah, Ahmad and Arjun saved an average of $51. Farah saved $13 more than Ahmad. Arjun saved twice as much as Ahmad. How much did Ahmad save?
items.e: Total = 3 × $51 = $153. 4 units + $13 = $153, so 4 units = $140 and 1 unit = $35. Ahmad saved $35.

items.q: The average Maths mark of a class of 40 pupils was 68. Later, the teacher found that one pupil’s mark of 54 should have been 94. What is the correct average mark of the class?
items.e: The total increases by 94 − 54 = 40. Shared among 40 pupils, the average increases by 40 ÷ 40 = 1. Correct average = 68 + 1 = 69.

items.q: The bar graph shows the rainfall at a weather station from July to November. The average monthly rainfall from July to December was 210 mm. What was the rainfall in December?
items.e: Total for 6 months = 6 × 210 = 1260 mm. July to November = 150 + 250 + 200 + 300 + 100 = 1000 mm. December = 1260 − 1000 = 260 mm.

items.q: The average of three numbers A, B and C is 60. A is twice as big as B. C is 3 times as big as B. What is C?
items.e: Total = 3 × 60 = 180. A + B + C = 2 units + 1 unit + 3 units = 6 units. 6 units = 180, so 1 unit = 30. C = 3 units = 90.

items.q: The average mass of 20 pupils is 40 kg. The average mass of the 8 boys among them is 43 kg. What is the average mass of the girls?
items.e: All: 20 × 40 = 800 kg. Boys: 8 × 43 = 344 kg. Girls: 800 − 344 = 456 kg for 12 girls. Average = 456 ÷ 12 = 38 kg.

items.q: Ethan saved an average of $4.50 a week for 8 weeks. How much must he save in the 9th week so that his average savings for the 9 weeks is $5.00?
The average of 8 numbers is 25. When 2 of the numbers are removed, the average of the remaining numbers is 22. What is the average of the 2 numbers that were removed?
items.e: Total of 8 numbers = 8 × 25 = 200. Total of the other 6 = 6 × 22 = 132. The 2 numbers add up to 200 − 132 = 68. Average = 68 ÷ 2 = 34.

items.q: The average of 5 consecutive even numbers is 36. What is the largest of the 5 numbers?
items.e: For numbers that go up in equal steps, the average is the middle number. The numbers are 32, 34, 36, 38 and 40. The largest is 40. (Check: 180 ÷ 5 = 36.)

items.q: Mei Ling, Raju and Ali had an average of $56 each. Mei Ling spent $18 and Raju was given $6. What is their new average amount of money?
items.e: Total before = 3 × $56 = $168. Total after = $168 − $18 + $6 = $156. New average = $156 ÷ 3 = $52.

items.q: In a quiz, the average score of a team of 6 pupils was 15 points. A 7th pupil joined the team and scored 22 points. How many more points did the 7th pupil score than the new average of the team?
items.e: Old total = 6 × 15 = 90. New total = 90 + 22 = 112. New average = 112 ÷ 7 = 16. Difference = 22 − 16 = 6.
